title: RxJS: the operators that pay for themselves, and when a signal is enough

videos.script:
Signals answer one question: what is it now. Some questions are about time instead: how long to wait, which answer is the newest, whether to try again. Those are the questions R X J S is for.

{{observables}} You start with an observable written by hand. It does nothing until somebody subscribes, and every subscriber starts it again.

{{operators}} Then operators, map, filter and take, which you learn to read as values drawn on a line of time.

{{switch}} A search box puts three of them together. Without a pause, every key sends a request, and debounce time cuts that down to one. Switch map makes sure an old answer never lands last.

{{interop}} To signal and to observable carry values between the two worlds, and the async pipe is what older code uses.

{{retry}} Then the planner's save learns to try again, but only for failures that may pass.

{{choose}} And you sort the tools: which questions want a signal, and which want R X J S.
